case_name: Mary Roy v. State of Kerala
key_principle: Declared Travancore/Cochin Christian Succession Acts void retrospective to 1951. Christian daughters have equal intestate succession rights as sons under the Indian Succession Act, 1925. Note: Partition challenges are strictly subject to 12-year limitation under Article 65 of Limitation Act from date of open ouster.
risk_trigger: Deeds post-1951 where property of an intestate Christian father was partitioned or sold without female siblings joining as executing parties.
remedial_action: Obtain registered Ozhivumuri (Release Deed) or Supplementary Partition Deed with female heirs as co-executants before token advance, unless clearly barred by long-standing ouster exceeding 12 years.
statute_reference: Indian Succession Act, 1925, Section 37; Limitation Act 1963, Article 65; Article 14 Constitution of India

key_principle: Under Section 23(1) of the Senior Citizens Act 2007, a transfer can be declared void ONLY IF the deed contains an EXPLICIT condition that the transferee shall provide basic amenities and physical needs. Merely reciting 'love and affection' is a motive, not a condition. Without an express condition, Maintenance Tribunal has no jurisdiction to revoke the deed.
risk_trigger: Threat of cancellation under Section 23 by elderly parents where gift/settlement deed lacks an explicit maintenance condition.
remedial_action: Inspect registered deed text: if no explicit clause mandating physical maintenance exists, subsequent purchaser is legally protected against Section 23 cancellation under Sudesh Chhikara.
statute_reference: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, Section 23(1)

key_principle: Section 23 of Senior Citizens Act 2007 requires an explicit or clearly ascertainable condition that the transferee shall maintain the senior citizen. If breach occurs and condition exists, RDO Tribunal can declare the transfer void.
risk_trigger: Title deeds where property was acquired via Gift Deed (Dhanam) or Settlement from elderly parents.
remedial_action: Inspect parent gift deed for maintenance recitals. Require senior citizen parent to be a concurring witness or sign an affidavit of satisfaction.
statute_reference: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, Section 23

case_name: State of Kerala v. Landowner (Paddy Fee Exemption)
key_principle: The 25-cent fee exemption under Section 27A applies strictly only if the total landholding is 25 cents or less. There is NO pro-rata deduction: if a parcel exceeds 25 cents, conversion fee must be paid on the ENTIRE extent. Anti-fragmentation rule: parcels fragmented from larger units after 30 Dec 2017 are ineligible for 0% fee.
risk_trigger: Plots claiming 25-cent free exemption where total holding exceeds 25 cents, or land was subdivided after 30 Dec 2017.
remedial_action: Calculate statutory conversion fee across entire plot extent if > 25 cents. Verify parent title for holding size as of 30 Dec 2017.
statute_reference: Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act, 2008, Section 27A; G.O.(P) No. 1166/2020/Rev

case_name: Sree Swayamprakash Ashramam v. G. Anandavally Amma
key_principle: Easement of necessity or quasi-easement: Pathway rights granted in earlier deeds run with the dominant heritage and cannot be unilaterally closed by subsequent purchasers.
risk_trigger: Recitals reserving 'Nadappu vazhi', 'Vazhi avakasham', or shared passage along northern/southern boundary.
remedial_action: Conduct physical boundary survey. If pathway exists, obtain written relinquishment release or factor reduced usable area.

key_principle: Daughters have equal coparcenary birthright in Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) ancestral property under Section 6 HSA, even if father passed away before 9 Sept 2005 amendment.
risk_trigger: Partition deeds or alienation of ancestral Hindu property without signature of living or deceased daughter's legal heirs.
remedial_action: Examine genealogy tree. Verify whether property was self-acquired or ancestral coparcenary property. Obtain release from all coparceners.

key_principle: Under Section 8(2) HMGA 1956, natural guardian cannot sell, gift, or mortgage minor's immovable property without prior permission of the District Court. Any unauthorized disposal is voidable at minor's instance.
risk_trigger: Prior deed where parents or guardian sold land on behalf of minors without mentioning District Court O.P. Sanction Order.
remedial_action: Verify whether minor has attained 21 years (3 years after turning 18). If within 3 years of majority, obtain registered ratification deed.
statute_reference: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956, Section 8(2)

citation: 1918 (45) IA 73 (Privy Council) & Mohd. Amin v. Vakil Ahmad (1952 AIR 358)
court: Privy Council / Supreme Court of India
key_principle: Under Mohammedan Law, a de facto guardian (such as mother or brother) has zero legal power or authority to alienate minor's immovable property. Such alienations are ab initio VOID.
risk_trigger: Sale deeds executed by Muslim mother on behalf of her minor children without appointment by Court under Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.
remedial_action: Sale is void. Fresh conveyance or registered ratification from the erstwhile minor upon attaining majority is strictly required.
statute_reference: Principles of Mohammedan Law; Guardians and Wards Act, 1890

case_name: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Haryana
key_principle: General Power of Attorney (GPA / Mukthiyar) or Agreement to Sell does not convey title or ownership. Immovable property can only be transferred by a registered deed of conveyance.
risk_trigger: Purchasing property on the basis of an unregistered or expired GPA, or where principal died prior to deed registration.
remedial_action: Ensure PoA is registered at SRO. If executed overseas, ensure stamping by Kerala District Collector within 3 months. Confirm principal is alive.
statute_reference: Transfer of Property Act 1882 Sec 54; Registration Act 1908 Sec 17; Powers of Attorney Act 1882

case_name: Kudikidappu Tenancy Rights (Kerala Land Reforms Act)
citation: Sections 75 to 80B, Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1963
court: Kerala High Court & Land Tribunal Precedents
key_principle: Kudikidappukars (hutment dwellers) possess permanent non-evictable statutory occupancy rights and purchase certificate rights up to 10 cents in Panchayats and 3 cents in Municipalities.
risk_trigger: Old family estates or ancestral parambus with unverified huts, caretakers, or agricultural workers residing on the land.
remedial_action: Conduct physical inspection of land for residential dwellings. Verify Revenue Land Tribunal register for unassigned Kudikidappu purchase certificates.

case_name: Doctrine of Lis Pendens (T.G. Ashok Kumar v. Govindammal)
key_principle: Under Section 52 of Transfer of Property Act, any transfer of property during pendency of a suit in court is subordinate to the rights of the decree holder.
risk_trigger: Discrepancies in revenue tax receipts, active boundary disputes, or unfiled court caveats.
remedial_action: Run EC cross-check for court attachment notices. Search Kerala e-Courts database for pending OS or CMA cases against seller.
statute_reference: Transfer of Property Act, 1882, Section 52; CPC Order 38 Rule 5

case_name: Adverse Possession vs. Government Puramboke (Joseph v. State of Kerala)
key_principle: No adverse possession can be claimed against Government Puramboke land, road alignments, or river/thodu boundaries. Kerala Land Conservancy Act empowers immediate eviction.
risk_trigger: Land where registered extent on paper is 12 cents but physical fencing encloses 15 cents adjoining a canal (thodu) or road puramboke.
remedial_action: Verify Village Survey Sketch and Taluk Resurvey FMB. Ensure purchase consideration only covers surveyed registered patta land.
statute_reference: Kerala Land Conservancy Act, 1957, Section 3 & Limitation Act 1963 Art 112

case_name: R.D.O. Fort Kochi v. Jalaja Dileep & Baby v. Collector
key_principle: Lands converted prior to 12-08-2008 and not included in Data Bank are 'Unnotified Lands'. Section 27A applies for BTR reclassification, with statutory exemption from fee up to 25 cents.
risk_trigger: Land described as Nilam or Nanja in Village BTR or Prior Deeds but physically appearing as garden land with grown trees.
remedial_action: Confirm exclusion from LLMC Data Bank via Village Office. Apply for Form 6 under Section 27A. Zero fee applies if <= 25 cents.
statute_reference: Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land & Wetland Act, 2008, Section 27A; Kerala Land Tax Act 1961 Sec 6A

case_name: Mary Roy v. State of Kerala
key_principle: Struck down Travancore Christian Succession Act 1092 ME. Declared that female Christian heirs have equal intestate succession rights in paternal property with retrospective effect from 1951. Partition deeds omitting daughters create fatal defective title.
risk_trigger: Christian family partition prior to 1986 or post-1986 where female coparceners or sisters did not sign.
remedial_action: Obtain registered rectification deed (Thiruthu aadharam) or release deed (Ozhivumuri) from omitted female heirs.
statute_reference: Indian Succession Act 1925 / Travancore Christian Succession Act

key_principle: Daughters become coparceners by birth with equal rights as sons under Section 6 of Hindu Succession Act. Coparcenary rights confer irrespective of whether the father was alive on 09 September 2005.
risk_trigger: Hindu ancestral or coparcenary property partitioned without adult daughters as co-executants.
remedial_action: Require all surviving daughters and their legal representatives to execute confirmation deeds.

key_principle: For Maintenance Tribunal (RDO) to cancel a settlement deed under Section 23 of Senior Citizens Act, the document must contain an express or implied covenant that the transferee is bound to provide basic amenities.
risk_trigger: Property acquired via settlement/gift deed from elderly parents without independent consideration.
remedial_action: Verify donor parent is alive and willing to join as consenting witness, or obtain affidavit of maintenance.
statute_reference: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act 2007 Section 23

case_name: State of Kerala v. Binu Chacko
key_principle: Statutory fee exemption for plots up to 25 cents under Section 27A applies strictly based on the unfragmented mother plot status as on 30.12.2017. Plots carved out after 2017 are ineligible for 0% fee.
risk_trigger: Small plot (<25 cents) that was carved out from a larger paddy land parcel after 30 December 2017.
remedial_action: Calculate 10% fair value conversion fee on entire extent and budget for Section 27A application.
statute_reference: Kerala Conservation of Paddy Land and Wetland Act 2008 Section 27A
